questions.question: Which sites or pages should the extension work on?
questions.why: Narrow page access keeps the scope clear.

questions.question: How does the user start it, from a toolbar, menu, or page itself?
questions.why: The entry point shapes the work flow.

questions.question: What should the person see change after running it?

exit_criteria: Name supported pages, user entry points and the action on each one.

questions.question: Which browsers do you actually need for the first release?
questions.why: Their store and permission rules differ.

questions.question: Is this only for your team or for anyone in a store?
questions.why: The answer determines how users get it.

questions.question: Who prepares screenshots, support details and privacy information?
questions.why: Someone should own each release requirement.

exit_criteria: Confirm browsers, distribution path and ownership of store submissions.

questions.question: Which exact browser permissions does the task need?
questions.why: The browser should ask only for required access.

questions.question: Will any page text, browsing history or account data leave the browser?
questions.why: Users need to understand what is sent and why.

questions.question: How can someone remove stored extension data?
questions.why: The plan needs a clear removal path.

exit_criteria: Explain why each permission is needed and describe the handling of any collected page data.

questions.question: What should the extension show when a user declines permission?
questions.why: People need to understand what still works.

questions.question: What happens if someone runs it on an unsupported page?
questions.why: The extension needs a clear, safe response.

questions.question: If the browser reloads a page in the middle, what work should be restored?
questions.why: A refresh should not cause duplicate or lost work.

exit_criteria: Describe empty, denied-permission and unsupported-page behavior.

release_check.procedure: Install the store release or load the unpacked release into a clean browser profile. Capture the installed extension and one successful core action.
